note: Deterministic rules. The LLM never decides what is flagged. Verify every source quote against the live page before a public demo.

rules.title: See a doctor about your symptoms — don't wait for routine screening
rules.reason: You reported {symptoms}. These can have many causes, including high blood sugar. Only a doctor can check what is going on.
rules.action: Book a GP visit in the next few days and mention these symptoms.
rules.whyShort: I reported symptoms that a doctor should check
rules.actionShort: See a GP in the next few days

source.name: HealthHub (MOH Singapore) — Diabetes
source.quote: Common symptoms of diabetes include excessive thirst, frequent urination, unexplained weight loss and blurred vision; see a doctor if you have them.

rules.title: You're due for a diabetes screening
rules.reason: You are {age}, and your last blood sugar test was {lastTest}. Screening is recommended every 3 years from age 40.
rules.action: Book a diabetes screening (blood test) at a Healthier SG / Screen for Life clinic.
rules.whyShort: I'm 40+ and haven't been screened in the last 3 years
rules.actionShort: Book a diabetes screening blood test

source.name: Health Promotion Board — Screen for Life
source.quote: Diabetes screening is recommended once every 3 years for Singaporeans aged 40 and above.

rules.title: Ask a doctor whether you should be screened earlier
rules.reason: Your {relativeList} has diabetes. A parent, brother or sister with diabetes is a known risk factor, so screening may be advised before 40.
rules.action: Do the Diabetes Risk Assessment and ask a GP if you should be screened now.
rules.whyShort: A close blood relative has diabetes
rules.actionShort: Ask a GP about screening before 40

source.name: Health Promotion Board — Screen for Life (adults 18–39)
source.quote: Singaporeans aged 18 to 39 are encouraged to complete the Diabetes Risk Assessment; those found at risk are advised to go for screening.

rules.title: Your weight-to-height ratio is a risk factor worth discussing
rules.reason: Your BMI works out to about {bmi}. For Asian adults, a BMI of 23 or more is linked to higher diabetes risk.
rules.action: Do the Diabetes Risk Assessment and ask a GP if you should be screened.
rules.actionShort: Ask a GP about screening before 40

source.name: HealthHub (MOH Singapore) — BMI for Asians
source.quote: For Asians, a BMI of 23 and above indicates increased health risk.

rules.title: Past gestational diabetes means regular screening
rules.reason: You told us you had diabetes during a pregnancy. That raises the chance of type 2 diabetes later, even years after.
rules.action: Book a diabetes screening blood test, and repeat at least every 3 years.
rules.whyShort: I had diabetes during a pregnancy
rules.actionShort: Book a diabetes screening blood test

source.name: American Diabetes Association — Standards of Care, Section 2
source.quote: People with a history of gestational diabetes should have lifelong testing for prediabetes and/or diabetes at least every 3 years.

treatedNotice: You told us you already take diabetes medicine. Screening nudges don't apply — keep following the plan from your doctor.
noNudgeNotice: None of the diabetes rules we check matched what you told us today. This is NOT an all-clear: it only covers diabetes screening timing, and things can change. Keep up regular check-ups, and see a doctor if you feel unwell.
